schema_ddl: CREATE TABLE R (A INT, B INT, C INT);
q1: SELECT X.B AS XB FROM R AS X WHERE X.A = 5 AND X.C < 1
q2: SELECT X.B AS XB FROM R AS X WHERE X.A < 10
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT X.B AS XB FROM R AS X WHERE X.A = 5 AND X.C < 1
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT X.B AS XB FROM R AS X WHERE X.A < 10
counterexample: INSERT INTO R (A, B, C) VALUES (5, 10, 5);
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not equivalent. Q1 filters rows where A = 5 and C < 1, while Q2 filters rows where A < 10. These conditions are not logically equivalent. Q1 is more restrictive than Q2, so there may be rows included in Q2 that are not included in Q1.
counterexample_dsp: A test database with a row where A = 5, B = 10, and C = 5 will be included in Q2 but not in Q1. This demonstrates the difference in the WHERE clauses.
